shouldFix.quotedSubjectText: G16V5-OBS-2 is one shared class with Claude Stage A notRaised naming-v6 path standing; both identifiers are preserved.
shouldFix.charge: The clause 'both identifiers are preserved' asserts that two named identifiers exist for this shared class and travel forward. Only one exists. Codex Stage A carries the identifier G16V5-OBS-2. The Claude Stage A counterpart is .notRaised[3], and .notRaised in that verdict is a four-element array of plain strings with no identifier scheme at all, so the naming-v6 path standing carries no Claude-side identifier. The entry therefore prints one identifier while claiming preservation of two.
measurement: docs/coop/artifacts/harness.DR-G16.ci-isolation-integration.v5.review-independent.claude2.json recomputes to 246993a8c653d129348b4a470e82cc5e68f7724d24406223391e1e9086f44602, the value the draft pins. Its top-level keys are artifact, subject, subjectSha256, subjectSha256Recomputed, subjectSha256Matches, subjectMode, subjectMoved, reviewer, date, discipline, verdict, blockers, mustFix, shouldFix, custody, priorFindingDisposition, attackSurfaceChecked, notRaised, decisionRule, verdictStatement, doesNot. There is no advisories key and no observations key.
.notRaised is a list of length 4; every element is a plain string (isinstance str == True for all four). No element carries an id field, and no identifier token of any scheme appears in the array.

.notRaised[3] is the shared-class member: 'gate-harness-naming.v6 .gates[15].artifactPathWhenAuthored still points at the v1 artifact and artifactExists is false. Cleared: naming v6 is frozen at D-145 and predates v2..v5; the subject states the two lineages are unrelated and does not restate the naming file's own fields as current.' Codex G16V5-OBS-2 reads 'Frozen gate-harness-naming.v6 still carries its at-authoring v1 path and artifactExists false.' Same class, confirmed; the draft's class identification is correct. Only the two-identifier claim is not.

The phrase is an established term of art in adopted COORD and is used exactly twice, both times with two named identifiers that the entry itself prints. COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md line 9169: 'CLAUDE-G31-V5-ADV-2 / CODEX-G31-V5-ADV-1 (one shared class; both identifiers preserved)'. Line 9475: 'CLAUDE-G14-V3-SF1 and CODEX-G14-V3-SF1 (one shared class; both identifiers preserved)'. In both precedents a Claude identifier and a Codex identifier exist and both appear in the entry. D-215 reuses the phrase where the Claude side has no identifier to preserve.

The draft names five Claude identifiers: CLAUDE-G16-V1-SF1, CLAUDE-G16-V3-MF1, CLAUDE-G16-V3-SF1, CLAUDE-G16-V4-MF1, CLAUDE-G16-V4-SF1. Each is charged at a different locus (liveCellMemberSplit.delimiter, executesVerbatim, authorityClaim, basedOn.namingV6.role, registerRowNote). None is the naming-v6 path standing. There is no Claude identifier anywhere in the lineage that a future auditor could resolve this clause to.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: The COORD entry is the durable record of which honesty identifiers travel forward from Stage A. An auditor who later resolves 'both identifiers are preserved' against Claude Stage A finds an unlabeled notRaised clearance and no identifier, and cannot tell whether a Claude identifier was dropped in the recording or never existed. This lineage charges naming-precision defects of exactly this magnitude: CLAUDE-G16-V3-SF1 was charged as SHOULD-FIX for a bare 'leftover-join.v3' token denoting the wrong join under the file's own convention, and CLAUDE-G16-V4-SF1 was charged as SHOULD-FIX for a roster field omitting v3. Reusing a two-identifier term of art for a one-identifier class is the same class of defect at the same magnitude.
shouldFix.notThisCharge: This is not a charge that the shared class was misidentified, that the Codex observation was dropped, that an observation was upgraded or downgraded, or that any honesty work was hidden. G16V5-OBS-1, G16V5-OBS-2, and G16V5-OBS-3 are all present and characterized correctly, and the shared class is disclosed rather than collapsed.
shouldFix.suggestedRepair: Reword the clause so the asymmetry is stated, for example: 'G16V5-OBS-2 is one shared class with the Claude Stage A notRaised naming-v6 path standing, which carries no identifier; the Codex identifier is preserved.' Scope-neutral: changes no digest, no count, no standing, no guard, and no authority.
shouldFix.scopeEffectOfRepair: NONE. Does not touch file 08, COORD, required-now, any leftover set, any digest, or any gate standing.
